title: All-team commencement checklist and exec brief
content:
Purpose:
This is a working checklist + executive briefing for the next company-wide commencement (Q1 planning + OKR kickoff). The doc is intended to be the single source for: run-of-show, speaker asks, rehearsal notes, pre-reads, and rapid contingency plans if execs are delayed or an agenda item needs to be cut.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: all employees (town-hall style) + remote contributors; executive and IC-level updates.
- Scope: 90-minute all-hands + 45-minute optional breakout tracks. Focus: company strategy recap, top-level OKR draft, cross-functional asks, and live Q&A.

High-level outcomes we want:
1) Everyone leaves with a concise sense of the top 3 company priorities for the quarter and 2 immediate team-level asks.
2) Executive alignment visible (all C-levels record a 2-3 slide update; product/eng show a single progress metric).
3) Enable follow-up: a clear comms plan, task owners, and a JIRA board seeded with 8 cross-org initiatives.

Pre-read package (to ship 4 days before event):
- Single-page company narrative (one-pager) that explains why each priority exists and what success looks like. (Owner: Aisha)
- Draft OKRs (top-level + suggested team mappings). (Owner: Liam)
- Two-slide exec updates (one metric, one ask). (Owners: Sofia + Jonah)
- How to participate guide (questions, polls, Slack channel). (Owner: comms)

Run-of-show (90 minutes):
- 00:00 – 00:05: Welcome + logistics (hosts: COO & VP People)
- 00:05 – 00:20: CEO strategy recap and vision framing (3 slides max)
- 00:20 – 00:35: Product & roadmap highlight (demo or short customer vignette)
- 00:35 – 00:50: OKR topline presentation (why these, success metrics, tradeoffs)
- 00:50 – 01:05: Engineering reliability/serving runtime update (latency and cost improvements)
- 01:05 – 01:20: Customer & GTM snapshot (adoption signals + partner asks)
- 01:20 – 01:35: People & org changes (hires, changes to on-call, hires pipeline)
- 01:35 – 01:45: Live Q&A + closing (moderated, upvoted questions first)

Optional breakout (45 minutes) — opt-in signups immediately after event:
- Track A: OKR translation workshop (product ops facilitated)
- Track B: Developer community & SDK roadmap (devex lead)
- Track C: Dedicated & Private customer readiness (solutions engineering)

Speaker asks and constraints (short, actionable):
- All exec slides must be no more than 3 slides, 2 minutes per exec, and one clear ask/outcome.
- Avoid deep technical demos during main session; put demos in breakout or follow-up video.
- Provide a 2-line TL;DR slide for each exec: the headline + one metric.

Rehearsal plan (owners and timing):
- Dry run 1 (leadership only): 3 days out. Goal: timing and slide glue. (Owner: Aisha + Executive EA)
- Dry run 2 (hosts + moderators + AV): 1 day out. Goal: transitions and Q&A flow. (Owner: comms + SRE on-call)
- AV checklist: dual-mic test, stream health, captions enabled, backup laptop with recorded slides. (Owner: SRE)

Contingency tree (quick reference):
- Exec delayed > 5 minutes: switch to pre-recorded 2-minute CEO message, proceed with next segment.
- Bandwidth outage (region): switch to audio-only + Slack thread for questions; post recording when recovered.
- Major incident for product (severity >= SEV2): postpone OKR deep-dive; run a 20-minute incident update and pivot to resilience messaging.

Measurement of success (post-event):
- Survey NPS-style question (was the session useful?) target >= 60% positive.
- Percent of teams who have mapped at least one top-level OKR to a team objective within 10 days (target 75%).
- Number of follow-up JIRA initiatives created (target >= 8).

Unresolved items / open decisions:
- Final OKR phrasing: product KR3 wording needs editorial pass (suggested owner: Liam).
- All-hands length vs. participation tradeoff: leadership prefers 75 min; comms prefers 90 min. Decision due by EOD 2025-11-12.
- Global-friendly timing: APAC-friendly slot will likely reduce live participation in NA. Proposal: run main at 09:30 PT and a posted recording with synchronous follow-up office hours at 18:00 SGT. Need final sign-off from People Ops.

Action list (immediate, owner, due):
- Publish pre-read one-pager (Aisha) — due 2025-11-07
- Collate exec slides into master deck (Sofia) — due 2025-11-07
- Seed JIRA board with cross-org initiatives (Jonah) — due 2025-11-10
- Schedule dry runs and calendar invites (Comms) — due 2025-11-06
- Build moderation queue in Slack and set up upvoting (Comms) — due 2025-11-09

Notes to self / facilitation hints:
- Keep energy high by opening with a 30-second customer anecdote.
- Use the Miro board for breakout capture; assign a scribe for each room.
- If we cut content, prioritize cutting the engineering micro-metrics rather than the CEO narrative.

Post-event comms plan (owners):
- Same-day: publish recording + one-pager + top 5 takeaways (Comms)
- 3 days: issue tracker with owners + first cut of team-to-okr mappings (Product Ops)
- 14 days: leadership follow-up email with adjustments to OKRs and decisions.

Risk register (top 5 risks and mitigations):
- Risk: Poor exec alignment visible on stage. Mitigation: mandatory leadership dry run and aligned speaking notes.
- Risk: Low engagement from remote offices. Mitigation: scheduled regional office-hours and follow-up office Q&A.
- Risk: Conflicting asks across teams leading to overloaded squads. Mitigation: cross-org intake board and prioritized gating.
- Risk: AV failure. Mitigation: recorded fallback + SRE standby.
- Risk: Post-OKR confusion. Mitigation: product ops will publish a mapping template and host office hours.

Appendix: suggested language for the opening slide (copyable):
"This quarter we focus on predictable, cost-efficient inference at scale. Our three priorities are: 1) Deliver Redwood Dedicated throughput guarantees, 2) Reduce host-per-token cost by 18% through batching and quantization, 3) Launch the Private VPC onboarding flow for our first 5 enterprise customers. Success means customers running production inference on our platform with <100ms p50 for the top 10% of requests and measurable MRR motion for Dedicated."

Notes on tone and style: concise, engineering-friendly, avoid marketing hyperbole in the main OKR framing. Where useful, add short customer quotes but keep the main slides metric-first.

If anything in here looks off or you want to propose a shorter run-of-show, add comments below or update the action owners section.
